extra.message: User input from 'username' parameter is directly interpolated into an SQL query using f-string formatting. This allows SQL injection attacks where attackers can bypass authentication, extract data, or modify the database.

User-controlled filename from 'name' parameter is passed directly to open() without validation or sanitization. This allows path traversal attacks (LFI) where attackers can read arbitrary files on the system.

User-controlled URL from 'name' parameter is passed directly to requests.get() without validation. This allows Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks where attackers can make requests to internal services or external systems.
SSL certificate verification is disabled with verify=False. This makes the application vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks as it will accept any SSL certificate without validation.
User input from 'mathexp' parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template and rendered. This allows Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) attacks that can lead to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: User input from 'username' parameter is reflected back in the response without sanitization or encoding. This allows Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks where malicious scripts can be injected and executed in victims' browsers.

The Host header from user request is used directly in HTML output within an anchor tag without sanitization. This allows HTTP Header Injection leading to XSS attacks and Open Redirect vulnerabilities.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site
